steps.title: Turn it on
steps.text_html: A Mappia map is described by a query: a list of layers, written in JavaScript. This one has a single layer, the states of Brazil - a published map named CSR:estados. It starts switched off, so the map is empty.

messages.layers.CSR:estados.visible: The States layer is still off: set visibility to true, then Run.

hints_html: visibility decides whether the layer is drawn when the map opens.
The line should read visibility: true, - lower case, no quotes.

steps.title: Give it a name
steps.text_html: title is the name the reader sees in the layer list and in the menus. name stays as it is: it points at the published map.
steps.task_html: Change the title to "States of Brazil" and Run.

messages.layers.CSR:estados.title: The title must read exactly States of Brazil - check the spelling and the capitals.
messages.layers.CSR:estados.visible: The layer is off again: keep visibility: true.

hints_html: Change only the text between the quotes after title:.
The line should read title: "States of Brazil", - text keeps its quotes.

steps.title: The reader decides
steps.text_html: Your query decides how the map opens: visibility: true means States of Brazil is drawn when the map starts. After that, whoever reads the map can switch each layer off and on with the map itself - the eye button on the layer's row, at the top left of the map, or Maps, the map's own menu bar along its top edge.
steps.task_html: No code this time. In the map on the right, hide States of Brazil with the eye button on its row, then show it again.

messages.reader: Use the map itself: hide States of Brazil with the eye button on its row (top left of the map), then show it again.
messages.pass: Done: you switched the layer with the map itself, and the query did not change - visibility: true only decides how the map opens.

hints_html: Look inside the map: at its top left, the row States of Brazil has an eye button. Click it once to hide the layer, once more to show it.
Or click Maps in the thin bar along the top edge of the map (not this page's menus), then the switch next to States of Brazil, twice.

steps.title: A name must exist
steps.text_html: name must be a map that the server publishes, written WORKSPACE:map. A name that is not in the catalogue is not drawn - the first thing to check when a layer is missing. Break it on purpose, to see the message you will get.
steps.task_html: Change the name to "CSR:does_not_exist", Run, and read the message. The next step puts the map back.

messages.warningSeen: The name still points at a real map: change the text after name: (not the title) to CSR:does_not_exist, then Run.

hints_html: Only the text inside the quotes after name: changes.
The line should read name: "CSR:does_not_exist",.

steps.title: One expression, not a program
steps.text_html: The platform does not run a query line by line: it reads the whole text as one expression, whose value is the list of layers. A statement such as var x = 1; before the list breaks it. This page catches that before anything reaches the map.
steps.task_html: Type var x = 1; on a new line just before the [ and Run: read the message. Then delete that line and Run again, so the map comes back.

messages.parseErrorSeen: The query ran without a problem. Type var x = 1; on its own line before the [ (not as a comment), then Run.
messages.parseErrorSeenNext: Good, that is the message. Now delete the line var x = 1; and Run again, so the map comes back.
messages.layers.CSR:estados.present: The states are not back on the map yet: keep their { } entry, delete only the line var x = 1;, then Run.
messages.pass: Done: a statement broke the query, and without it the query is one expression again - the map is back.

hints_html: Put the cursor at the start of the [ line, type var x = 1; and press Enter, then Run.
After the message, delete the whole line var x = 1; - the query starts with the [ again - and Run.

steps.title: A second layer
steps.text_html: A map is usually several maps on top of each other. Each entry of the list, between { }, is one layer, and entries are separated by commas. The first entry is drawn on top: the relief you add will cover the state borders - the next step fixes that.
steps.task_html: Add { name: "CSR:altimetria", title: "Elevation", visibility: true } as the first entry of the list, then Run.

messages.layers.CSR:altimetria.above: Elevation is drawn under the states: move its { } entry before the States entry - the first entry of the list is drawn on top.
messages.layers.CSR:altimetria: There is no Elevation layer on the map yet. Its name is CSR:altimetria - copy it exactly.
messages.layers.CSR:altimetria.visible: Elevation is in the list but switched off: add visibility: true to it.
messages.layers.CSR:estados: The States layer went missing: keep its { } entry in the list.
messages.layers.CSR:estados.visible: The States layer is off: keep its visibility: true.

hints_html: Copy the whole { ... }, block of the states, paste it right after the [, then change its name and title.
Between the two { } blocks there must be a comma: }, then {.

steps.title: Half transparent
steps.text_html: opacity goes from 0 (invisible) to 1 (opaque) - a fraction, not a percentage. Below 1, what is under the layer shows through: here the state borders and the basemap's towns, under the relief.
steps.task_html: Make the Elevation layer half transparent, then Run.

messages.layers.CSR:altimetria.opacity: The Elevation layer's opacity must be between 0.3 and 0.7: 0 is invisible, 1 is opaque (it is not a percentage).
messages.layers.CSR:estados.visible: The States layer is off: keep its visibility: true.

hints_html: Add a property to the Elevation entry - the one on top - next to its visibility.
Add the line opacity: 0.5, inside the Elevation { } - a number, without quotes.

steps.title: A layer the reader turns on
steps.text_html: A layer can start switched off and wait in the top menu until the reader wants it. That keeps the first view simple. Here: the forest biomass of the Amazon.
steps.task_html: Add { name: "CSR:biomassa_baccini_bioma_am", title: "Forest biomass (Amazon)", visibility: false } at the end of the list and Run. Then switch it on from Maps, the menu bar along the top edge of the map - a layer that is off has no row with an eye button yet.

messages.layers.CSR:biomassa_baccini_bioma_am: The biomass layer is not on the map yet: add its { } entry at the end of the list, with a comma before it.
messages.reader: Leave it off in the query, then switch on Forest biomass (Amazon) from Maps, the menu bar along the top edge of the map.

hints_html: The new { ... }, entry goes just before the final ]; - check there is a comma after the } above it.
Keep visibility: false in the query; the switch in Maps turns it on.

steps.title: Names come from the catalogue
steps.text_html: The map server publishes a catalogue of its maps, each with a name such as CSR:altimetria. A layer's name must be one of them, copied exactly. Each map also covers its own region. Some names in this tutorial's catalogue: CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade (slope, Cerrado), CSR:biomassa_baccini_bioma_am (forest biomass, Amazon), CSR:precip_annual_average (annual rainfall, Mozambique).
steps.task_html: Add the slope of the Cerrado, CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade, titled "Slope (Cerrado)", as the first entry - on top of the others - and Run.

messages.layers.CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade: There is no slope layer on the map yet. Copy its name exactly: CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade.
messages.layers.CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade.vis: The slope layer is switched off: add visibility: true.

hints_html: Names are copied from the catalogue, not guessed: workspace, colon, map.
Right after the [, add { name: "CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade", title: "Slope (Cerrado)", visibility: true },.

steps.title: A group in the top menu
steps.text_html: A real map has dozens of layers; groups organise them. A group with a title becomes an entry of the top menu, and its layers go in elements, a list like the query itself.
steps.task_html: Wrap the States layer in { title: "Boundaries", elements: [ ... ] }, Run, and open Boundaries in the top menu.

messages.layers.CSR:estados.menu: States is not under Boundaries in the top menu yet: the group needs title: "Boundaries" and elements: [ ... ] around the layer.
messages.layers.CSR:estados: The States layer went missing: its whole { } entry goes inside elements: [ ... ].

hints_html: The group is an entry of the list too: { title: "Boundaries", elements: [ before the States block, ] }, after it.
Inside elements: [ ... ] the States block stays exactly as it was.

steps.title: A heading in the layer panel
steps.text_html: A group with viewTitle instead of title is a heading in the layer panel, above those of its layers that are on. openGroup: true starts it expanded.
steps.task_html: Wrap Elevation and Slope in { viewTitle: "Terrain", openGroup: true, elements: [ ... ] } and Run.

messages.layers.CSR:altimetria.panel: Elevation has no Terrain heading in the layer panel: use viewTitle: "Terrain" (a title makes a top-menu entry instead).
messages.layers.CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade.pan: Slope is not under the Terrain heading: put its { } entry inside the same elements: [ ... ] as Elevation.
messages.layers.CSR:estados.menu: Keep the Boundaries group of the previous step around States.

hints_html: One group holds both layers: { viewTitle: "Terrain", openGroup: true, elements: [ before Elevation, ] }, after Slope.
Use viewTitle, not title: title makes a top-menu entry.

steps.title: Groups inside groups
steps.text_html: Groups nest: a group's elements can hold layers or other groups. A top-menu group around the Terrain heading gives both - an entry in the top menu and a heading in the panel. Its color colours the menu entry and the rows of its layers.
steps.task_html: Put the whole Terrain group inside { title: "Relief", color: "#8d4925", elements: [ ... ] }, Run, and open Relief in the top menu.

messages.layers.CSR:altimetria.menu: Elevation is not under Relief in the top menu: wrap the Terrain group in { title: "Relief", elements: [ ... ] }.
messages.layers.CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade.men: Slope is not under Relief in the top menu: it belongs in the Terrain group, inside Relief.
messages.layers.CSR:altimetria.panel: Keep the Terrain heading: the whole { viewTitle: "Terrain", ... } group goes inside Relief's elements.
messages.layers.CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade.pan: Keep the Terrain heading: the whole { viewTitle: "Terrain", ... } group goes inside Relief's elements.

hints_html: The same move as Boundaries, one level up: Relief's elements holds the Terrain group.
{ title: "Relief", color: "#8d4925", elements: [ before { viewTitle: "Terrain", and ] }, after the Terrain group's closing },.

steps.title: Properties a group shares
steps.text_html: defaultProperties on a group is given to every layer inside it - unless the layer sets the property itself. Use it for what a whole theme shares: an opacity, a starting state.
steps.task_html: Give the Terrain group defaultProperties: { visibility: false, opacity: 0.7 } and Run. Elevation keeps its own visibility: true.

messages.layers.CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade.opa: Slope did not get the shared opacity: put defaultProperties: { ... } on the Terrain group, next to its viewTitle.
messages.layers.CSR:altimetria.opacity: Elevation did not get the shared opacity: defaultProperties goes on the Terrain group, which holds it.
messages.layers.CSR:altimetria.visible: Elevation should stay on: its own visibility: true wins over the group's default.
messages.layers.CSR:bioma_cerrado_declividade.vis: Slope should start off: the group's defaultProperties sets visibility: false.

hints_html: defaultProperties is a property of the group, next to viewTitle and openGroup.
Add the line defaultProperties: { visibility: false, opacity: 0.7 }, under openGroup: true,.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.text_html: That is the core of every Mappia map: layers with a name and their properties, organised in groups. This last step has no task to check - change anything you like and Run. The next chapters (servers, calculated maps, controls) build on this map.
steps.task_html: Change any title, opacity or group, Run, and look at the map. Copy the query when you are happy with it.
hints_html: Try a new color for Relief, or another opacity for Boundaries.
If something breaks, the message says which line - and the last working map stays on screen.

parse.message: The query is empty. A query is a list of layers: it needs at least [ and ].
The query is not complete: a ], } or quote is still open. Every [ needs its ], every { its }.
The query is not complete: a ], } or quote is still open. Every [ needs its ], every { its }.

Line {line}: a query is one expression - the list of layers - so it cannot contain a statement like `{token} ...;`. Values shared by the query are declared with setQueryGlobalProperties, joined to the list with &&.
Line {line} closes with {token}, but something above is not closed the same way. Check that every { has its } and every [ its ], in that order.
Something is missing at the end of line {prevLine} - often a comma. Each property, and each layer { }, ends with a comma.
Line {line}: inside { } a property ends with a comma, not a semicolon.
Line {line}: this {token} does not match an opening bracket - one too many here, or one missing before it.
Line {line}, near `{token}`: this is not valid here. Text needs quotes ("like this"), and each property ends with a comma.
Line {line}: curly quotes ({char}) come from word processors. Type straight quotes (") instead.
Line {line}: the character {char} is not allowed here.
Line {line}: a text has no closing quote. Add the " at its end.
Line {line}: a /* comment is never closed with */.
Line {line}: a number is followed by letters. A number has digits only (0.5); text goes in quotes.
Line {line}: write a colon between a property and its value (title: "States"), not an equals sign.
Line {line}: `{word}` is a reserved word of JavaScript and cannot be used here.
Line {line}: the query is not valid JavaScript here ({original}).

runtime.message: Line {line}: JavaScript only knows true, false and null in lower case - `{name}` is not one of them.
Line {line}: `{name}` is not a value Mappia knows. Text needs quotes ("{name}"); a name shared by the query must be declared before the list, with setQueryGlobalProperties.

runtime.match: ^TypeError: [\w$.]*\.map is not a function|is not iterable
runtime.message: The query must end with the list of layers [ ... ]. In an && chain, the last part is the list.
Line {line}: `{name}` is not a function Mappia has. Check its spelling - the API reference lists them.
Line {line}: the query reads `{name}` from something that does not exist (yet).
The map could not run the query: {original}

warnings.match: Could not create layer record for layer '(?<typed>[^']+)'
warnings.message: There is no map called {typed} in the catalogue - check its spelling.
The map server "{name}" did not answer - this is not your mistake. Press Run again in a moment.
The layers of the server "{name}" are left out because it did not answer.
